title: Cone Crusher

introduction.definition: A cone crusher crushes rock between a gyrating mantle and a fixed concave (bowl liner). The main shaft sits in an eccentric bushing; as the eccentric turns, the mantle moves closer to and away from each part of the concave in turn. Rock is squeezed repeatedly as it moves down the chamber and leaves through the closed-side setting.
applications: Secondary and tertiary crushing of aggregates and ore
key_points: Product size set by CSS (hydraulic or screw adjustment)
Reduction ratio typically about 3–6 : 1 per stage
introduction.summary: A cone crusher crushes rock between a gyrating mantle and a fixed concave. The eccentric bushing, turned by a bevel gear, makes the head gyrate (wobble) so the gap opens and closes around the circle; rock is squeezed repeatedly as it moves down to the closed-side setting.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Capacity and product size depend on CSS, eccentric throw and speed; choke-fed chambers give more inter-particle crushing and better shape.

wear.title: Concave and mantle wear profile
wear.description: Wear is heaviest in the lower (parallel) zone, where the particles are smallest, the gap is closest and the crushing force is concentrated (purple). As the liners wear the closed-side setting opens, so it is re-adjusted (hydraulic or screw adjustment) to hold product size; liners are changed when the profile can no longer hold the setting or capacity drops.

foundation: Mount on a massive reinforced-concrete foundation or steel structure designed for the crusher's dynamic loads (maker's load data); use anti-vibration mounts where specified.
Allow crane access and lay-down space for liner and wear-part changes.
alignment: Align motor and crusher sheaves or coupling; set V-belt tension to the maker's figure.
Set the closed-side setting (CSS) or gap with the maker's gauge/lead-ball method.
piping: Feed with a controlled feeder (choke or regulated feed as designed); avoid segregated or one-sided feed.
Fit a tramp-metal magnet or metal detector ahead of the crusher and dust extraction at transfer points.
Lubrication system: connect oil supply/return, cooler and filter; check flow and pressure switches.
commissioning: Check lubrication flows and temperatures before starting; run empty to check direction, vibration and current.
Introduce feed gradually; measure product size and adjust the setting; record power draw as a baseline.

routine.task: Check oil flow, pressure and temperature; listen for knocking.

periodic.task: Measure CSS and liner wear; adjust setting.

overhaul.task: Replace mantle and concaves; inspect eccentric bushing and gears.

lubrication: Circulating oil system: check filter ΔP, oil analysis, cooler performance.

remedies: Adjust setting; replace liners; distribute feed evenly

symptoms: High oil temperature, low pressure alarm
remedies: Fix system; never run without oil flow

causes: Tramp metal, packing, too small setting
remedies: Remove tramp; increase setting; regulate feed

safety: Lock out; release hydraulic clearing/clamping pressure before maintenance; use proper lifting tools for mantle/bowl.

video_tutorials.title: Cone Crusher — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Cone Crusher.
A cone crusher crushes rock between a gyrating mantle and a fixed concave (bowl liner).
The main shaft sits in an eccentric bushing; as the eccentric turns, the mantle moves closer to and away from each part of the concave in turn.
Rock is squeezed repeatedly as it moves down the chamber and leaves through the closed-side setting.
Typical applications include secondary and tertiary crushing of aggregates and ore; producing cubical aggregate; pebble crushing in grinding circuits.

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Cone Crusher Shell / Bowl (top & bottom), Eccentric Bushing & Bevel Gear (rotates → head gyrates), Countershaft, Bevel Pinion & V-Belt Sheave, Main Frame / Bottom Shell (discharge opening).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Cone Crusher works.
Feed enters the top and falls into the chamber.
The pinion drives the eccentric; the eccentric makes the mantle gyrate.
The mantle approaches each part of the concave in turn, squeezing the rock.
Product passes the closed-side setting at the bottom.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Wear is heaviest in the lower (parallel) zone, where the particles are smallest, the gap is closest and the crushing force is concentrated (purple).

video_tutorials.title: Cone Crusher — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Cone Crusher.
Check oil flow, pressure and temperature; listen for knocking.
Measure CSS and liner wear; adjust setting.
Replace mantle and concaves; inspect eccentric bushing and gears.
Watch for liner wear: product coarsening, falling capacity. Common cause: normal abrasion, uneven feed.
Watch for lubrication failure: high oil temperature, low pressure alarm. Common cause: pump/filter/cooler fault, contaminated oil.
Watch for ring bounce / overload: bowl lifts, loud bangs. Common cause: tramp metal, packing, too small setting.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
